title: You thought it was just a delay.
paragraphs: You thought it was just a delay.
Just a rough season. A bad year. Maybe even a string of unfortunate choices you keep trying not to think about when the room goes quiet.
But then you read it—and it didn’t read you gently.
“I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten…” — Joel 2:25
Years.
Not moments. Not days.
Years.
And something in you tightened, because you knew exactly what those years held.

The nights you said, “Just this once.”
The mornings you woke up already tired of yourself.
The quiet compromises no one else saw.
The calling you kept postponing.

God saw it.
You knew.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this isn’t a verse you skim and move on from. It stops you. It forces you to confront a truth most people spend their lives avoiding.

You didn’t just lose time.
Something ate it.
Joel doesn’t soften the language. He names it: locusts. Destruction. Consumption. Devouring forces that leave nothing but emptiness behind. And if you’re honest, you’ve felt that.

Time that should have built you… hollow.
Opportunities that should have matured you… wasted.
Moments meant for obedience… replaced with delay.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God didn’t just promise to restore what was lost.
He promised to restore what was eaten.
There’s a difference.

Lost things can be found.
Eaten things are gone.
Or at least, that’s what logic says.
But Scripture doesn’t operate on your logic.
It confronts it.
Because right before that promise, God says something even heavier:
“I sent among you the locust…” — Joel 2:25 (earlier context)
Read that again.
Some of what you lost wasn’t random.
It was allowed.
Not to destroy you—but to wake you.

Because you kept ignoring the quiet conviction.
You kept silencing the warnings.
You kept choosing comfort over surrender.
So God let the emptiness speak louder.
And it did, didn’t it?

That feeling that something’s off.
That you’re behind.
That you’ve drifted further than you ever intended.
That’s not just regret.
That’s exposure.
And this is where most people break.

They either drown in guilt…
Or numb themselves into distraction.
But Joel doesn’t leave you there.
He brings you to a turning point that cuts through every excuse:
“Return to Me with all your heart…” — Joel 2:12

Not partially.
Not later.
Not when life calms down.
All your heart.
Because restoration doesn’t begin when time is fixed.
It begins when your heart is surrendered.
You want those years back?
Then face what consumed them.

Sin wasn’t harmless.
Disobedience wasn’t neutral.
Delay wasn’t safe.
It cost you.
But here’s where the Gospel steps in—and everything shifts.
Because the same God who exposed your loss… made a way to redeem it.
Not through your effort.
Not through trying to “do better.”
Through Jesus Christ.
“He restores my soul…” — Psalm 23:3
Not your schedule.
Your soul.
Because the real damage wasn’t the calendar.
It was the condition of your heart.
And Jesus didn’t come just to give you better years.
He came to give you a new life.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
That means the years you think disqualified you…
Don’t have the final word.
The shame you keep replaying…
Doesn’t define you anymore.
The destruction you thought was permanent…
Can be reversed in ways you can’t explain, only experience.
But it won’t happen while you stay where you are.
You can’t hold onto the life that drained you and expect God to restore what it took.
You already know that.
You’ve felt it.
That tension inside you right now—that pull between staying comfortable and finally surrendering—
That’s your moment.
Not tomorrow.
Now.
Because there are still two futures in front of you.
One where you keep scrolling, keep delaying, keep telling yourself you’ll change eventually…
And one where you actually return.
Fully.
Honestly.
Without pretending.
And here’s the truth you can’t ignore anymore:
God is willing to restore.
But He will not compete with your excuses.
If this hit something real in you, don’t brush it off like everything else.
Say it plainly.
“I need restoration.”
Not the kind you fake for others.
The kind only God can do.
There’s more waiting for you than wasted years—but you won’t see it from a distance.
Walk toward it.
Stay close to this. There’s depth you haven’t touched yet, correction you need, clarity you’ve been missing.
Follow this path if you’re done repeating the same cycles.
